resources.string: Bluetooth is off — turn it on in the phone settings
Key database: loaded, CRC %1$s, Mobile Application ↔ Insulin Pump
No internet or the page did not answer
advertising for pairing — pair on the pump now
waiting for the pump to come back
On the 780G the pump often drops the link for about a minute right after the first pairing and comes back — wait.
Pairing with the other name: the phone\'s Bluetooth name is changed while the pairing goes on, then it comes back.
The pump does not list the phone? Try another name: for the pairing the phone\'s Bluetooth name is changed for a while, and it comes back right after.
Stop MiniMed Mobile on this phone: Settings → Apps → MiniMed Mobile → Force stop (two \"Mobile\" apps get in each other\'s way).
The phone waits for the already paired pump (no pairing). Keep this screen open.
To stop the link, turn Permanent operation off.
The phone is waiting for the pump: %1$s (usually up to a minute — do not stop earlier)

Pairing did not finish. On the pump, open Options → Device Options → Managed Devices → Pair Device again and pick %1$s. On the phone, confirm the pairing request (it may come as a notification). No request? Turn Bluetooth off and on; if that does not help, restart the phone. The phone keeps waiting by itself: connecting usually takes up to a minute, so do not stop it early.
This phone has no Bluetooth LE: permanent operation is not possible.
To turn it on, turn Bluetooth on (quick settings at the top of the screen).
This phone cannot advertise over Bluetooth LE, so the pump cannot connect to it: permanent operation is not possible.
To turn it on, the pump\'s key database is needed: under Diagnostics press Download key database (needs the internet), or load it from a file there.
A pairing is going on: wait until it ends, or press Stop, then turn it on.
On: the phone keeps the link to the pump in the background and writes its boluses, carbs and basal to the journal.

The app will stay linked to the pump in the background and write its boluses, carbs and basal to the journal. MiniMed Mobile must not be connected to the pump at the same time. The app only reads the pump and never changes anything on it. It is not a medical device: check doses on the pump.
Bluetooth for the sensor is off in this app. Then Android may close the app in the background and pump data will stop coming. Turn on Use Bluetooth in this app\'s sensor Bluetooth settings.
The saved pump history could not be read. It is being collected again.
The phone has forgotten the pump

The pump is marked as paired, but it is no longer in the phone\'s Bluetooth list, so no data can come. Press Pair again, then on the pump open Options → Device Options → Managed Devices → Pair Device and pick %1$s, and confirm the request on the phone (it may come as a notification). No request? Turn Bluetooth off and on; if that does not help, restart the phone.
The phone stops waiting for a new pairing and goes back to waiting for the already paired pump. Use it if the pump did not start the pairing.
Pump history from before you turned it on
Found before you turned it on: boluses %1$d, meals %2$d
Nothing to write: everything found is already in the journal or older than the boundary. Either button closes this card; nothing old is written in both cases.
Older ones not in the journal, will not be written: %1$d
Carbs that will not be written (carb writing is off, or their bolus is not written): %1$d
New pump data is written in any case. This choice is only about the old records.
The list changed — check it again.
Write was not taken: the list changed before it got through. Check the new list and press Write again.
No answer from the app yet. If this card is still here, press again; if it repeats, share the journal.
Do not write the old records?
The pump records from before you turned it on will not be written to the journal. New ones are written as usual. This cannot be undone in the app.
the pump did not give its serial number, nothing kept
The first full read of the pump history is not finished yet
Boluses waiting for their start record (written by themselves once it is read): %1$d
The pump\'s clock differs from the phone\'s. Times in the journal follow the pump: set the time on the pump.
Some pump records are dated in the future. Check the date and time on the pump.
The pump has not said how much of a bolus was actually given. Check that bolus on the pump and in the journal.

A bolus was read without its start record yet. It goes to the journal by itself once the rest of the pump history is read; nothing to do. If this stays for hours, check that bolus on the pump and in the journal.
Carbs were found without a matching bolus. Check them in the journal.
Also writes the pump\'s serial number, doses and other values. For finding faults; usually off.

The journal file holds detailed lines: the pump\'s serial number, names and addresses of Bluetooth devices, the pump\'s answers and values. Share it only with someone you trust. To remove them, turn Detailed journal off and press Clear journal (share it first if you need it).
Share it first if you need it — clearing cannot be undone.

For MiniMed 7xx pumps (740G, 770G, 780G). Checked on a 740G (MMT-1811, firmware 6.28.3) with a Samsung phone on Android 14; on the 770G and 780G only by what other projects report (OpenMinimed), not checked by us.
This is not a medical device and it only shows data: the app reads the pump and never changes anything on it. Make dose decisions by the pump\'s own screen.

MiniMed Mobile has to be unpaired from the pump. Then the CareLink cloud (reports for the doctor, family following your data) stops getting data, and the pump\'s notifications no longer come to the phone — the pump beeps by itself.
SmartGuard auto mode and filling the reservoir are not checked: their records may not reach the journal, or may come in as boluses.

To go back to MiniMed Mobile: turn Permanent operation off, on the pump unpair \"Mobile\" with six digits (Managed Devices), forget the pump in the phone\'s Bluetooth settings, and pair MiniMed Mobile again.
This phone cannot advertise over Bluetooth LE, so the pump cannot connect to it.
Pair the pump with this phone
On the pump: Options → Device Options → Managed Devices — unpair MiniMed Mobile (leave the sensor alone).
Press Start pairing below. Then on the pump, in the same menu lower down, choose Pair Device and pick %1$s.
On the pump: Options → Device Options → Managed Devices → Pair Device — pick %1$s.
On the phone, confirm the pairing request (it may come as a notification in the shade). It usually takes up to a minute: do not stop it earlier, and keep this screen open.
The first start needs the internet once: the pump\'s key database is downloaded from the OpenMinimed page.
The key database did not download: %1$s. Check the internet and press Retry, or load the file key_databases.md of the OpenMinimed Documentation page.
Turn on Permanent operation: the phone then stays linked to the pump in the background and writes its boluses, carbs and basal to the journal. Pair again only if the phone has lost the pump.
It usually comes within a minute; after an app update or a phone restart it can take longer.
Do not remove the pairing in the phone\'s Bluetooth settings: if it is really gone, this window will say so.
Bluetooth is off, so no pump data can come. Turn it on (quick settings at the top of the screen).
The pump is not being called for now

Less than %1$d min is not offered: the pump brings its data about every 8 minutes and the check runs every 5, so a shorter wait would warn while all is well. An older choice of 5–15 min works as %1$d min.
The pump\'s own alarms do not come to the phone: the pump beeps by itself.
Link stage, buttons, values, link journal — for finding faults
older than 30 min (%1$s) — check the pump

Another app (for example, OMRON connect) got hold of Bluetooth before JugglucoNGmod. If the pump connected now, it would get stuck, and after 30 seconds the phone would erase its pairing. So the app does not call the pump: the pairing is safe, but no pump data comes for now. Turning Bluetooth off and on helps fastest (the sensor and the watch drop off for a moment). Otherwise the app checks every 5 minutes and brings the connection back by itself once the other app closes.
Most likely the pump will get stuck on the other app, and after 30 seconds the phone will erase the pairing — then the pump has to be paired again. Call the pump?
Turn Bluetooth off and on first, then go on with the pairing on the pump: another app got hold of Bluetooth before JugglucoNGmod, and the pairing may fail.

The phone erased the pairing itself: the pump got stuck on another app using Bluetooth (for example, OMRON connect). So turn Bluetooth off and on first, and only then press \"Pair again\" — otherwise the pairing fails the same way.
OMRON connect is installed: its Bluetooth server may get in the pump\'s way. If it is not yet among the deep sleeping apps in the phone\'s battery settings, add it there.
